annotations.note: 9M26 rev CZK 238.5bn, EBITDA CZK 86.1bn (-17%), NPAT CZK 26.6bn (+24%), net debt CZK 236.0bn (2.0x).
Revenues secured by long-term Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) or regulated tariff frameworks, providing hard-currency indexation and guaranteed minimum volume off-take.
Heavy generation transition capex peaks in 2024-2025; multi-year FCF inflects strongly positive as commercial operations commence.
Strategic national utility champions benefit from government balancing accounts or explicit fuel supply guarantees, mitigating commodity price volatility.
9M26 EBITDA CZK 86.1bn (-17% YoY, FY26 guide CZK 109-114bn reaffirmed); net debt +14% YTD to CZK 236.0bn (2.0x vs 1.5x).

verdict.stance: Neutral / Reaffirmed CZK 109-114bn Guide Amid Capex Leverage Creep (2.0x)
verdict.summary: ČEZ 9M26 net income jumped 24% YoY to CZK 26.6bn on the expiry of the Czech windfall tax even as EBITDA eased 17% to CZK 86.1bn on lower power realizations; net debt rose 14% YTD to CZK 236bn (2.0x vs 1.5x prior year) on transition capex.

positives: A-/A3 IG credit anchored by 70% Czech state ownership and regulated distribution/low-cost nuclear fleet.
Reaffirmed FY26 EBITDA guidance of CZK 109-114bn.
Manageable 2.0x net leverage despite heavy investment cycle.
negatives: Power-price normalization shaved 9M26 EBITDA by -17% YoY (CZK 86.1bn).
Heavy nuclear/grid capex pushed net debt +14% YTD to CZK 236.0bn (2.0x vs 1.5x).
Potential Dukovany new-nuclear financing / Czech state buyout structural uncertainty.
